answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a refundable bond before it may transact. Like a climber trusting a narrow ledge only after testing its weight, the network trusts an agent only after real stake is at risk: misbehavior burns the bond, so spawning a thousand fake selves costs a thousand real deposits. The pledge is recorded as durably as veins in onyx, honest agents recover their stake in full, and no identity gets dyed cheap like saffron water.
